extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the Department of Energy Computational Science Graduate Fellowship (DOE CSGF)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for applying to the DOE CSGF, including eligibility (citizenship and academic status), Program of Study (POS) rules, transcripts, references, track selection, and other application policies. Intended to help applicants prepare a complete, compliant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply and be considered you must be either a United States citizen or a Lawful Permanent Resident (LPR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no exceptions to the citizenship status rule. DACA/Dreamer status residents and student-visa residents are not eligible. Questions about citizenship eligibility can be sent to csgf@krellinst.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of permanent residency
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of a current and non-expired green card is required as part of the application; must hold permanent, non-conditional status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An I-551 stamp or letter will not suffice as proof of residency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic status eligibility — allowed categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants include undergraduate seniors (who will begin graduate school fall 2022), first-year graduate students (began graduate school fall 2021), master's degree students (subject to conditions), matriculating students beginning graduate program fall 2022, and certain employed/other classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is based on start of graduate school, not start of PhD program or thesis work. There is no limit to the number of times you can apply provided you remain eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic status exclusion — second-year students
rubrics_metrics.description: Second-year graduate students are not eligible regardless of receiving or not receiving a master’s degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defer to the university academic status of the applicant to determine eligibility; must be a full-time student on site at a U.S. accredited university. Questions about academic status eligibility can be sent to csgf@krellinst.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master's-degree applicant conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Master's degree students may be eligible only under specific conditions regarding PhD enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be attending a different institution for PhD, or may stay at same institution if pursuing a new department and new academic advisor, or if there is at least a two-year gap between completing the master’s degree and starting graduate school for PhD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time on-site enrollment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows must be full-time students on site at a U.S. accredited university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is used to determine eligibility; contact csgf@krellinst.org for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track selection: Traditional vs. Math/CS
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must choose between the traditional track and the math/CS track (math/CS track addresses DOE needs for research contributing to effective use of high-performance computer systems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must decide which track to apply to; the Program Coordinator cannot tell you the track you should apply for. Essay questions differ slightly; all other requirements and obligations are the same. Hint: research with an application → lean traditional; research without application → lean math/CS. Accepted fields are listed on the DOE CSGF website. Questions to csgf@krellinst.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program of Study (POS) — institution basis
rubrics_metrics.description: POS is based on the applicant's top-choice institution for students currently applying to graduate school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read instructions, guidelines, requirements, help links, and FAQ before emailing about the POS.

rubrics_metrics.name: POS course-count requirements (quarter vs semester)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quarter-system universities require 10 courses (3 courses in each section; 1 course in HPC section). Semester-system universities require 7 courses (2 courses in each section; 1 course in HPC section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you place courses in the correct POS sections per system.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-performance computing (HPC) course requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: POS must include an HPC course that introduces the concepts of HPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HPC course may be taken from any department with preference to CS; it cannot be double-counted as meeting both the HPC requirement and the requirements of any of the other three topic areas. Requirement may be waived with evidence of a suitable graduate-level course already completed. The HPC course should be added to the HPC section of the POS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course departmental/source requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All courses must come from their respective departments and be taken for graduate credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CS courses from CS department, math courses from math/stats department, science/engineering courses from science/engineering departments. Cross-listed courses acceptable. Interdisciplinary departments acceptable (e.g., EECS, CME, CSE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on POS completion prior to fellowship start
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than half of the POS may be completed before the start of the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: first-year graduate students may have their major area completed before the start of the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic advisor involvement with POS
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may use their current academic advisor or contact a potential advisor at their top-choice university to review the POS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See FAQ for more details; additional POS questions can be sent to csgf@krellinst.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation requirement and process
rubrics_metrics.description: Three letters of recommendation are required; a fourth slot is available but gives no advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter request that is sent to references is available within the application. Letters will be accepted after the application deadline, but it is the applicant's responsibility to check application status regularly and re-notify references if needed. Reference status indicators include: Notified, Submitted, Not notified, In progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcripts — official submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcripts must be official and sent directly from the university either through an e-transcript system or mailed, not sent by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-transcripts should be sent to csgf_trans@krellinst.org. Transcripts emailed, mailed or faxed by the applicant will not be accepted. Some exceptions exist for international transcripts—email DOE CSGF Program Coordinator if international university cannot send transcript. If applying to multiple fellowships administered by Krell Institute, only one copy of transcript is needed. If transcript name differs from application name or transcript will not be available by Jan 31, 2022 deadline, email the Program Coordinator. Transcript processing time may take 2–3 days; university fulfilment may take weeks. Hint: e-transcripts are preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component importance and strict requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each aspect of the application matters—POS, essay questions, letters of recommendation, and experience are important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship is very competitive and prestigious. Deferrals are not offered. POS and the 12-week practicum are strict requirements of the fellowship; no exceptions are made. Applicants should read all application documents, instructions, help links, and FAQ before emailing the Program Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application frequency policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit to the number of times you can apply for the fellowship provided that you remain eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure ongoing eligibility before reapplying; check citizenship and academic status rules each cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and help procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about eligibility, application details, or unique circumstances should be directed to csgf@krellinst.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read available online resources (instructions, help links, FAQ) before emailing. Specific transcript email: csgf_trans@krellinst.org for e-transcripts.
